name: Chronic Kidney Disease Management in Primary Care
:LABEL: Curriculum
description: Understand the fundamentals of managing chronic kidney disease in primary care

name: Definition, Diagnostic Criteria and Initial Work-up for CKD
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Define CKD as kidney damage or eGFR less than 60 mL/min/1.73m2 persisting for 3 months or more, irrespective of underlying cause;Identify evidence of kidney damage as albuminuria (ACR greater than 3 mg/mmol), persistent haematuria after exclusion of urological causes, structural abnormalities on imaging, or pathological abnormalities on biopsy;Explain that CKD diagnosis requires at least 2 abnormal results at least 3 months apart to confirm chronicity and exclude acute kidney injury;List initial work-up investigations as serum creatinine with eGFR, urine ACR, urine microscopy, electrolytes including potassium and bicarbonate, full blood count, HbA1c, lipids, and renal ultrasound if indicated;Identify indications for renal ultrasound as stage 4 or 5 CKD, suspected obstruction, family history of polycystic kidney disease, persistent haematuria, or rapid decline in kidney function;Recognize that eGFR can be affected by acute illness, dehydration, high protein intake, and muscle mass, requiring clinical context for interpretation
description: Understanding definition, diagnostic criteria and initial work-up for ckd: Define CKD as kidney damage or eGFR less than 60 mL/min/1.73m2 persisting for 3 months or more, irrespective of underlying cause

name: Risk Factors and Screening for CKD in Australian Primary Care
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: List major risk factors requiring regular screening as diabetes mellitus, hypertension, established cardiovascular disease, family history of kidney failure, and obesity with BMI 30 kg/m2 or greater;Identify additional risk factors as age 60 years or older, current smoking, Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, and history of acute kidney injury;Explain that Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples aged 30 years or older should be screened annually regardless of other risk factors;Recommend Kidney Health Checks every 1 to 2 years for people with risk factors, and annually if diabetes or hypertension is present;Recognize that early detection through systematic screening in at-risk populations allows intervention to slow CKD progression and reduce cardiovascular risk
description: Understanding risk factors and screening for ckd in australian primary care: List major risk factors requiring regular screening as diabetes mellitus, hypertension, established cardiovascular disease, family history of kidney failure, and obesity with BMI 30 kg/m2 or greater

name: The Kidney Health Check and Confirmation of Abnormalities
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Describe the three components of a Kidney Health Check as blood test for eGFR calculated from serum creatinine, urine test for albumin to creatinine ratio, and standardized blood pressure measurement;Explain that reduced eGFR less than 60 mL/min/1.73m2 requires confirmation with at least 2 measurements at least 3 months apart;State that elevated urine ACR requires confirmation with 2 out of 3 elevated measurements over at least 3 months using first morning void samples where possible;Identify confounders for urine ACR as urinary tract infection, menstruation, vigorous exercise within 24 hours, and acute febrile illness;Recognize that a sustained reduction in eGFR of 25% or more or an absolute drop of more than 5 mL/min/1.73m2 within one year may indicate acute kidney injury and requires urgent review within 7 days
description: Understanding the kidney health check and confirmation of abnormalities: Describe the three components of a Kidney Health Check as blood test for eGFR calculated from serum creatinine, urine test for albumin to creatinine ratio, and standardized blood pressure measurement

name: CKD Staging System Using eGFR and Albuminuria Categories
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Classify CKD by eGFR into stages: G1 is 90 or greater, G2 is 60 to 89, G3a is 45 to 59, G3b is 30 to 44, G4 is 15 to 29, and G5 is less than 15 or on dialysis;Classify albuminuria into categories: A1 is ACR less than 3 mg/mmol, A2 is ACR 3 to 30 mg/mmol, and A3 is ACR greater than 30 mg/mmol;Explain that stages G1 and G2 require evidence of kidney damage such as albuminuria, haematuria, or structural abnormalities to be classified as CKD;Recognize that full CKD specification combines eGFR stage, albuminuria category, and underlying diagnosis, for example CKD G3aA2 due to diabetic kidney disease;Understand that both lower eGFR and higher albuminuria independently increase risk of progression to kidney failure and cardiovascular events
description: Understanding ckd staging system using egfr and albuminuria categories: Classify CKD by eGFR into stages: G1 is 90 or greater, G2 is 60 to 89, G3a is 45 to 59, G3b is 30 to 44, G4 is 15 to 29, and G5 is less than 15 or on dialysis

name: Blood Pressure Management and Measurement in CKD
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: State the recommended blood pressure target for most people with CKD as below 130/80 mmHg based on standardized clinic measurement;Recognize that blood pressure targets should be individualized considering age, frailty, orthostatic symptoms, albuminuria level, and patient preferences;Explain that home blood pressure monitoring or ambulatory blood pressure monitoring provides more accurate assessment than clinic readings and targets are typically 5 mmHg lower;Identify that standardized blood pressure measurement requires patient seated quietly for 5 minutes, back supported, feet flat on floor, arm at heart level, and appropriate cuff size;Understand that blood pressure control is a key modifiable factor to slow CKD progression and reduce cardiovascular risk
description: Understanding blood pressure management and measurement in ckd: State the recommended blood pressure target for most people with CKD as below 130/80 mmHg based on standardized clinic measurement

name: RAAS Blockade as First-Line Therapy in CKD with Albuminuria
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Identify ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers as first-line antihypertensive agents for people with CKD and albuminuria category A2 or A3;Explain that RAAS inhibitors provide kidney protection beyond blood pressure lowering by reducing intraglomerular pressure and albuminuria;Recognize that an initial decline in eGFR of up to 30% within 2 to 4 weeks of starting RAAS inhibitors is acceptable if it stabilizes and does not indicate treatment failure;State that serum creatinine and potassium must be checked within 1 to 2 weeks after initiating or increasing dose of RAAS inhibitors;Identify that RAAS inhibitors should be ceased if eGFR falls by more than 30%, potassium rises above 6.0 mmol/L despite management, or bilateral renal artery stenosis is suspected
description: Understanding raas blockade as first-line therapy in ckd with albuminuria: Identify ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers as first-line antihypertensive agents for people with CKD and albuminuria category A2 or A3

name: SGLT2 Inhibitors and GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in CKD Management
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Identify SGLT2 inhibitors as indicated for people with CKD and type 2 diabetes, or for those with CKD and albuminuria regardless of diabetes status, where eGFR is 20 mL/min/1.73m2 or greater;Explain that SGLT2 inhibitors reduce risk of CKD progression, cardiovascular events, and hospitalization for heart failure;Recognize that SGLT2 inhibitors should be temporarily ceased during sick days with vomiting, diarrhea, or reduced oral intake to prevent volume depletion and ketoacidosis;Identify GLP-1 receptor agonists as providing cardiovascular and potential kidney benefits in people with type 2 diabetes and CKD;State that common adverse effects of SGLT2 inhibitors include genital mycotic infections, urinary tract infections, and volume depletion, requiring patient education and monitoring
description: Understanding sglt2 inhibitors and glp-1 receptor agonists in ckd management: Identify SGLT2 inhibitors as indicated for people with CKD and type 2 diabetes, or for those with CKD and albuminuria regardless of diabetes status, where eGFR is 20 mL/min/1.73m2 or greater

name: Glycaemic Management in CKD with Diabetes
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: State that HbA1c target for most people with diabetes and CKD is generally 53 mmol/mol or 7% or less, individualized to range 48 to 58 mmol/mol or 6.5% to 7.5%;Explain that glycaemic targets require individualization based on hypoglycaemia risk, life expectancy, duration of diabetes, established complications, and patient preferences;Recognize that HbA1c may underestimate glycaemia in advanced CKD due to shortened red cell survival and erythropoietin use;Identify that several glucose-lowering medications require dose adjustment or cessation as eGFR declines, including metformin, sulfonylureas, and SGLT2 inhibitors;State that metformin should be used with caution when eGFR is 30 to 44 mL/min/1.73m2 and ceased when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73m2 due to lactic acidosis risk
description: Understanding glycaemic management in ckd with diabetes: State that HbA1c target for most people with diabetes and CKD is generally 53 mmol/mol or 7% or less, individualized to range 48 to 58 mmol/mol or 6.5% to 7.5%

name: Lipid Management and Cardiovascular Risk Reduction in CKD
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Recommend statin or statin with ezetimibe combination for all people aged 50 years or older with any stage of CKD regardless of baseline cholesterol level;Identify indications for statin therapy in people younger than 50 years with CKD as presence of coronary disease, previous ischaemic stroke, diabetes mellitus, or estimated 5-year cardiovascular risk greater than 15%;Explain that CKD is an independent cardiovascular risk factor and traditional risk calculators may underestimate risk in people with CKD;State that no specific target serum cholesterol level is recommended for lipid management in CKD, with focus on statin use rather than treat-to-target approach;Recognize that cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in people with CKD, making comprehensive cardiovascular risk management essential
description: Understanding lipid management and cardiovascular risk reduction in ckd: Recommend statin or statin with ezetimibe combination for all people aged 50 years or older with any stage of CKD regardless of baseline cholesterol level

name: Lifestyle Modifications Including Diet, Exercise, Smoking and Alcohol
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Recommend a varied diet rich in vegetables, fruits, wholegrain cereals, lean meat, fish, legumes, and low-fat dairy, limiting salt intake to less than 6g per day or 100 mmol per day;Advise limiting foods high in saturated fats, added sugars, and avoiding high-calorie sweetened carbonated beverages;State that dietary protein intake should generally be maintained at 0.75 to 1.0 g per kg body weight per day, with restriction only under dietitian supervision in advanced CKD;Recommend 150 to 300 minutes of moderate intensity physical activity or 75 to 150 minutes of vigorous intensity activity per week, plus muscle strengthening on at least 2 days;Advise complete smoking cessation with support through counselling, nicotine replacement therapy, or other medications, and limiting alcohol to 2 standard drinks or less per day;Identify that potassium and phosphate restriction may be required in stage 4 and 5 CKD, requiring referral to accredited practising dietitian
description: Understanding lifestyle modifications including diet, exercise, smoking and alcohol: Recommend a varied diet rich in vegetables, fruits, wholegrain cereals, lean meat, fish, legumes, and low-fat dairy, limiting salt intake to less than 6g per day or 100 mmol per day

name: Monitoring Frequency and Parameters by CKD Stage
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Specify that CKD stage G3a requires monitoring of eGFR, urine ACR, electrolytes, and blood pressure every 6 to 12 months;State that CKD stage G3b requires monitoring every 3 to 6 months, adding full blood count and consideration of calcium, phosphate, and parathyroid hormone;Identify that CKD stage G4 requires monitoring every 3 months including full blood count, calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone, and bicarbonate;Recognize that CKD stage G5 requires monitoring every 1 to 3 months with nephrology co-management and preparation for renal replacement therapy;Explain that monitoring frequency should be increased if albuminuria is in A3 category, eGFR is declining, or complications develop
description: Understanding monitoring frequency and parameters by ckd stage: Specify that CKD stage G3a requires monitoring of eGFR, urine ACR, electrolytes, and blood pressure every 6 to 12 months

name: Medication Safety, Dose Adjustment and Nephrotoxin Avoidance
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Identify NSAIDs as nephrotoxic medications that should be avoided in CKD or used only short-term with close monitoring if essential;Recognize the triple whammy combination of RAAS inhibitor plus diuretic plus NSAID as particularly high risk for acute kidney injury;Explain that many medications require dose adjustment based on eGFR including antibiotics, antivirals, direct oral anticoagulants, opioids, and gabapentinoids;State that contrast media used in CT scans and angiography can cause contrast-induced nephropathy, requiring risk assessment, hydration, and temporary cessation of metformin and SGLT2 inhibitors;Identify that patients should be counselled to avoid nephrotoxic over-the-counter medications including NSAIDs and to inform all healthcare providers of their CKD diagnosis
description: Understanding medication safety, dose adjustment and nephrotoxin avoidance: Identify NSAIDs as nephrotoxic medications that should be avoided in CKD or used only short-term with close monitoring if essential

name: Sick Day Management and Acute Kidney Injury Prevention
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Explain that all patients with CKD should have a written sick day action plan for episodes of vomiting, diarrhea, fever, or reduced oral intake;List medications to temporarily cease during sick days as RAAS inhibitors, diuretics, NSAIDs, metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, and potentially other antihypertensives;Advise patients to maintain hydration during acute illness, continue essential medications, and seek medical review if unable to maintain fluids or symptoms persist beyond 24 to 48 hours;Recognize that people with CKD are at increased risk of acute kidney injury during intercurrent illness due to reduced renal reserve;State that medications should be restarted once the patient is well, eating and drinking normally, with repeat kidney function testing within 1 week
description: Understanding sick day management and acute kidney injury prevention: Explain that all patients with CKD should have a written sick day action plan for episodes of vomiting, diarrhea, fever, or reduced oral intake

name: Management of Common CKD Complications: Anaemia, Mineral Bone Disorder, Acidosis and Hyperkalaemia
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Define anaemia in CKD as haemoglobin less than 130 g/L in males or less than 120 g/L in females, requiring investigation with iron studies, B12, and folate before considering erythropoietin therapy;Recognize that mineral and bone disorder in CKD requires monitoring of calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone, and vitamin D from stage G3b onwards, with management including phosphate binders and vitamin D supplementation;Identify metabolic acidosis as serum bicarbonate less than 22 mmol/L, which accelerates CKD progression and may require oral sodium bicarbonate supplementation;Define hyperkalaemia as serum potassium greater than 5.5 mmol/L, requiring assessment for causes, dietary potassium restriction, medication review, and consideration of potassium binders;Explain that severe hyperkalaemia greater than 6.5 mmol/L or any hyperkalaemia with ECG changes requires urgent same-day management or emergency department referral
description: Understanding management of common ckd complications: anaemia, mineral bone disorder, acidosis and hyperkalaemia: Define anaemia in CKD as haemoglobin less than 130 g/L in males or less than 120 g/L in females, requiring investigation with iron studies, B12, and folate before considering erythropoietin therapy

name: Indications for Nephrology Referral
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Identify that CKD stage G4 with eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73m2 or stage G5 requires routine referral to nephrology for co-management and preparation for renal replacement therapy;List urgent referral indications as rapidly declining eGFR with sustained fall of more than 25% or more than 5 mL/min/1.73m2 per year, or eGFR fall of more than 15 mL/min/1.73m2 within 3 months;Recognize that persistent albuminuria category A3 with ACR greater than 30 mg/mmol despite optimal management warrants nephrology referral;Identify that persistent haematuria with proteinuria, suspected glomerulonephritis, suspected genetic kidney disease, or systemic disease affecting kidneys requires specialist assessment;State that resistant hypertension despite 3 or more antihypertensive agents, recurrent nephrolithiasis, or suspected obstructive uropathy are additional referral indications
description: Understanding indications for nephrology referral: Identify that CKD stage G4 with eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73m2 or stage G5 requires routine referral to nephrology for co-management and preparation for renal replacement therapy

name: Renal Replacement Therapy Options and Shared Decision Making
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: List the main renal replacement therapy options as facility haemodialysis, home haemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and kidney transplantation;Identify that conservative management focused on symptom control and quality of life is an appropriate option for selected patients with stage G5 CKD;Explain that kidney transplantation offers the best survival and quality of life outcomes for suitable candidates with stage G5 CKD;Recognize that shared decision making and advanced care planning should commence when eGFR is around 20 to 25 mL/min/1.73m2, well before dialysis is required;Understand that treatment decisions should consider patient values, preferences, comorbidities, frailty, life expectancy, and social circumstances
description: Understanding renal replacement therapy options and shared decision making: List the main renal replacement therapy options as facility haemodialysis, home haemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and kidney transplantation

name: Patient Education, Self-Management and Culturally Safe Care
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Explain to patients what CKD is, what their stage means, and that early intervention can slow progression and reduce complications;Educate patients about medication adherence, home blood pressure monitoring, recognizing sick days, and when to seek medical help;Provide counselling on avoiding nephrotoxic over-the-counter medications, maintaining hydration, and importance of regular monitoring;Recognize that Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples experience disproportionately high rates of CKD and require culturally safe, community-engaged approaches to care;Identify barriers to care including health literacy, language, geographic isolation, and socioeconomic factors, and work with patients to develop individualized management plans;Understand the importance of involving family, utilizing Aboriginal health workers, and coordinating with multidisciplinary team members including nurses, dietitians, and pharmacists
description: Understanding patient education, self-management and culturally safe care: Explain to patients what CKD is, what their stage means, and that early intervention can slow progression and reduce complications

name: Pregnancy Considerations and Teratogenic Medications in CKD
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Identify that women of childbearing age with CKD require preconception counselling regarding pregnancy risks, which increase with lower eGFR and higher albuminuria;Recognize that RAAS inhibitors including ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers are teratogenic and must be ceased before conception;List other medications requiring review before pregnancy as statins, some antihypertensives, and immunosuppressants in transplant recipients;Explain that pregnancy in CKD requires specialist nephrology and high-risk obstetric co-management due to increased risks of preeclampsia, preterm delivery, and accelerated kidney function decline;State that women with CKD planning pregnancy should have optimization of blood pressure control with pregnancy-safe agents, typically methyldopa, labetalol, or nifedipine
description: Understanding pregnancy considerations and teratogenic medications in ckd: Identify that women of childbearing age with CKD require preconception counselling regarding pregnancy risks, which increase with lower eGFR and higher albuminuria

name: Vaccination and Infection Prevention in CKD
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Recommend annual influenza vaccination for all people with CKD;Advise pneumococcal vaccination according to Australian immunization guidelines, with consideration of revaccination in advanced CKD;Identify that hepatitis B vaccination is indicated for people with stage G4 or G5 CKD in preparation for potential dialysis, with post-vaccination serology to confirm response;Recognize that people with CKD, particularly those on immunosuppression or dialysis, are at increased risk of infections;Explain that COVID-19 vaccination is strongly recommended for all people with CKD as they are at higher risk of severe disease
description: Understanding vaccination and infection prevention in ckd: Recommend annual influenza vaccination for all people with CKD

name: Red Flags Requiring Urgent Assessment or Same-Day Referral
:LABEL: Concept
understanding_criteria: Identify rapidly rising creatinine with eGFR fall of more than 25% or absolute fall of more than 15 mL/min/1.73m2 within 3 months as requiring urgent assessment within days;Recognize severe hyperkalaemia greater than 6.5 mmol/L or any hyperkalaemia with ECG changes as requiring same-day emergency department referral;List other urgent indications as acute pulmonary oedema, suspected nephritic syndrome with haematuria and acute kidney injury, malignant hypertension, or suspected obstructive uropathy with anuria;Identify that nephrotic syndrome with heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, and oedema requires urgent nephrology referral within days;Recognize that these presentations may represent rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, acute interstitial nephritis, or other conditions requiring immediate specialist assessment and treatment
description: Understanding red flags requiring urgent assessment or same-day referral: Identify rapidly rising creatinine with eGFR fall of more than 25% or absolute fall of more than 15 mL/min/1.73m2 within 3 months as requiring urgent assessment within days
